title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders
summary: The method replaces per-layer and per-round KV caching in looped language models with an asymmetric causal encoder-decoder in which a recurrently looped encoder refines a single globally shared KV cache via stochastic-depth training to a fixed point, eliminating round-wise cache growth. The cost is a full architecture change and a training procedure with stochastic recurrence depth, which is incompatible with simply reusing an existing pretrained decoder-only checkpoint and adds training complexity. It can fail if the fixed-point equilibrium does not hold for a given task or depth distribution, degrading long-context quality, and the serving numbers were validated only at 552B-parameter scale on a 4xGB200 node, so benefits at smaller scales are unverified.
rationale: The technique requires training or substantially modifying a model architecture, which exceeds the reader's constraint of no foundation-model training, and its production evidence comes from hardware (a 4xGB200 node serving a 552B model) the reader does not have.
technique: Recurrent-depth encoder-decoder with shared KV cache

claims.statement: The method replaces per-layer and per-round KV caching in looped language models with an asymmetric causal encoder-decoder in which a recurrently looped encoder refines a single globally shared KV cache via stochastic-depth training to a fixed point, eliminating round-wise cache growth. The cost is a full architecture change and a training procedure with stochastic recurrence depth, which is incompatible with simply reusing an existing pretrained decoder-only checkpoint and adds training complexity. It can fail if the fixed-point equilibrium does not hold for a given task or depth distribution, degrading long-context quality, and the serving numbers were validated only at 552B-parameter scale on a 4xGB200 node, so benefits at smaller scales are unverified.

The Looped CED holds 36.8x less KV per token than a conventionally looped model, matches the unlooped model's 38 concurrent 128K-token requests, recovers 86-93% of a looped Transformer's quality gain with 1/6 of its global KV, and serves 3.6x higher throughput on 8K-token prompts.
